constraints: Implementation is authorized only within the scope admitted by the future admission warrant; any expansion requires a separate proposed and admitted plan.
Field names and semantics follow ABS-0004 v8 exactly; deviations require an ABS revision first.
All relations use the GraphRelation shape; no predicate outside the registered Slice A, B, and C lists.
authorize() is pure over stored records: no I/O, no clock, no network; the decision timestamp is supplied by the caller.
Slice A capture and Slice B resolution behavior are unchanged: no field, path, or default of either is altered.
Standing authority may not be asserted implicitly. A principal record must declare its authority_scope, and an authorization outside that scope is refused rather than downgraded.
expected_outputs: ai_lab/governance/roles.py (role, qualification, and principal schemas with validators).
ai_lab/governance/authorization.py (authorization records, pure authorize(), consequence classification, governed/experimental classifier, one-hop self-adjudication check).
docs/self_model/PREDICATE_REGISTRY.md extended with the Slice C predicates.
docs/self_model/AUTHORIZATION_RECORDS.md documenting the record family, the standing-authority termination rule, and stated limitations including the one-hop bound.
tests/test_roles.py and tests/test_authorization.py with schema, rejection, refusal-reason, and integration fixtures.

Seed records: the operator's AccountablePrincipal record and the role definitions AI-Lab already uses in practice (drafting actuator, comparison advisor, adjudicating principal, deterministic verifier).
mitigation: Both limits are stated in the documentation and in the capability record rather than left to inference: governed means an authorization covers the invocation, and the self-adjudication check is one hop. Refusal reasons are enumerated so that a permitted outcome is never a silent default. The role vocabulary is copied from ABS-0004 v8 verbatim rather than invented, and the seed roles describe practice already visible in the record. The fourteen refusal reasons replace the original six: COMP-0037 found four missing, and COMP-0043 found three further defects in the resulting ten. authorize()'s valid authorization means only that an authorization record covers the invocation; it does not certify disclosure compliance, and the Section 4.7 constraints are expressly excluded from what is checked. Success criteria are restated to claim only enumerated-fixture coverage rather than universal properties, per the same round's finding that 'never fails silently' and 'is monotonic' are not mechanically checkable as written. Party sameness is decided on exact identifier equality only, and the documentation states that broader sameness is not detected.
next_action: WITHDRAWN under DECISION-20260727-0002 together with ABS-0004 v8, on which its semantics depend. A replacement plan should implement descriptive records and neutral assessment outputs only, and should not emit the terms governed or valid authorization: the COMP-0118..0125 round established that an invocation with undisclosed subordinate execution can earn both. It should follow the admission of a reconstructed ABS-0004 v9, not precede it. The prior wording of this field presupposed its own approval, which an adjudication checkpoint must not do.
non_goals: Refusing or blocking any execution. Authorization classifies; it does not gate. Execution refusal requires a separately admitted plan.
Routing, escalation, or model selection (RoutingDecision remains deferred).
Multi-hop lineage traversal, independence assessment, or evidence admission (Slice D).
Retroactive authorization of invocations captured before this slice; they remain experimental, and the pre-provenance boundary applies.
Any claim that the one-hop check implements C3. It implements C3's most direct case only, and the documentation must say so.
Automatic consequence assignment from artifact content; consequence is declared per authorization with the default derived from target type.
Cryptographic attestation of principals; ABS-0004 records it as a later implementation mechanism, not an ontology requirement.

Any claim that AI-Lab validates a standing-authority declaration. Per ABS-0004 v8 P7, root authority is extra-systemic: the system records the claim and cannot verify it, and no record, scope grammar, or internal approval step may be presented as verification.

Refusing a self-issued authorization. Self-issue is marked and disqualified from independence, not blocked: at the root of any chain the accountable party necessarily authorizes work it is responsible for.

Any claim that check_depth prevents a consumer from misreading a permitted result. It records the scope of the check that ran. Preventing the misreading would require either a consumer that refuses to treat a direct-only permitted result as evidence of adjudicator independence, or Slice D's ancestry traversal.
objective: Make the authority separation AI-Lab has practised in conversation structural: who may perform what, under which role, at what consequence, on whose standing authority, recorded as evidence rather than as testimony. The immediate motivation is concrete: on 2026-07-23 a model-default change would have set the reviewer slot to the drafting executor's own identity, collapsing reviewer and author under C3. Nothing in the system would have noticed; it was caught because a human happened to be told. Slice C makes the most direct case of that collision detectable by machine.
proposed_change: After a separate admission checkpoint, and after ABS-0004 v8 is admitted: add ai_lab/governance/roles.py (RoleDefinition, RoleQualification, AccountablePrincipal schemas and validators), ai_lab/governance/authorization.py (InvocationAuthorization records, the pure authorize() function, consequence classification, the experimental-versus-governed classifier, and the one-hop self-adjudication check), predicate-registry entries, documentation, and tests. No change to provider-call behavior, no change to Slice A capture or Slice B resolution, and no refusal of any execution.
rationale: ABS-0004's enforcement matrix records C6 authority separation as 'adopted, not currently evidenced': no artifact names the check. Slice C supplies the role records the matrix names as C6's activation dependency. It does not supply an enforcement artifact: the one-hop check is identity-based, not axis-based, and does not touch C6's restriction on exercising authority outside an assigned role. For the C6 row to cite enforcement evidence rather than a satisfied dependency, Slice C would additionally need to produce and retain named artifacts identifying the invocation or target, the role assignment relied on, and the separation actually checked. It does not.
The near-miss of 2026-07-23 is the exhibit: identity collision between reviewer and author was invisible to every test, and was avoided by chance rather than by control.

Slice A supplies produced_by and executed_by, so a one-hop identity collision is detectable now without the ancestry traversal that belongs to Slice D. The cheap case is available; the expensive case stays deferred.

ABS-0004 v8 fixes where authorization chains terminate - at an AccountablePrincipal's recorded standing-authority claim within a declared scope - and states plainly that this does not close the bootstrap regress. The open question remains open. v8 does not claim that no internal control could close it: it records that none is known to survive either COMP-0037 construction, and that whether some other could is unresolved. An earlier revision of this plan attributed the stronger claim to v7, which v7 did make and v8 withdrew. The constraint supplies visibility of the declared, not prevention. What is settled before any code depends on it is the termination rule and an honest account of its limits, not a resolution of the regress.

COMP-0037 split: one reviewer recommended revise-first, the other admit-with-conditions, and both independently defeated v6's chain termination. They did so by DIFFERENT constructions: one declared a scope wide enough to cover the intended invocation, the other declared one narrowly tailored to authorize exactly itself. Both also recommended mechanical scope bounding. This plan previously described them as constructing "the same self-authorization path", which under-reported the round and was the same mischaracterization ABS-0004 v8 corrected in its own [OPEN] paragraph. Because the two constructions run in opposite directions, breadth is not the property at fault; what they share is that the declarant fixed its own scope. v8 declines the scope-bounding recommendation for that reason and records the declining. v8 does not claim that no internal control could answer the break; it records that none is known to survive either construction, and makes the coincidence of issuer and executor visible instead.
risk: An authorization system that classifies but never refuses can create a false sense of control: readers may assume governed means checked when it means covered by a record. The one-hop self-adjudication check has the same hazard at a finer grain, since it will pass every deeper collision. Role and consequence vocabularies decided here are load-bearing for Slice D's admission rules, and a coarse role taxonomy would propagate. Beyond those: v8 makes the honest limitation explicit rather than closing it, so a reader who wants an assurance AI-Lab cannot give will find the system declining to give it, which is correct and may be mistaken for a defect. v8 also records that its self-issued disqualification is inert until AuthorizationPolicy exists, so this slice must not present the self_issued marking as a control. The self_issued marking depends on identifying when two records name the same party, which is straightforward for exact identifiers and undecidable in general; the implementation must not claim to detect sameness it cannot establish.
scope: A roles module defining schema v1 for RoleDefinition (task_function, epistemic_authority, action_authority, and the constraint fields ABS-0004 4.9 enumerates), with a validator, canonical serialization, and deterministic identity and path rules under docs/roles/.

RoleQualification records, execution-scoped as ABS-0004 4.6 requires: qualified executor, role, service endpoint scope, permitted ExecutionProfile constraints, session-state constraints, policy version, and the evaluation evidence relied on. A qualification never transfers implicitly to another endpoint or a materially different profile, and the validator rejects a qualification lacking an execution scope.
AccountablePrincipal records with principal_id, principal_kind, authority_scope, and delegation_reference, carrying no personal identifying data.

InvocationAuthorization as a DecisionRecord kind: invocation request, authorized executor, assigned role, consequence class, applicable policy, qualifications relied on, independence requirements, conditions, issuing principal, and the standing-authority or chained-authorization reference that terminates its chain.

A pure authorize() function over stored records returning an authorization outcome or one of the enumerated refusal reasons: (1) no qualification for this executor and role; (2) qualification out of execution scope; (3) consequence above the role ceiling; (4) unterminated authorization chain; (5) standing authority claimed outside its declared scope; (6) an authorization condition is unmet; (7) the authorization is malformed; (8) required conditions are absent; (9) authorized executor does not match the executor performing the invocation; (10) the authorization or a record it relies on is inactive or superseded; (11) subordinate execution represented as an Invocation but outside the classes its parent authorization declares; (12) self-adjudication conflict; (13) no authorization record covers this invocation; (14) an independence requirement recorded on the authorization is unmet. Fourteen reasons, each with a fixture. COMP-0037 found four missing from the six originally proposed. COMP-0043 found three further defects in the resulting ten: reasons 6 to 8 above were a single reason combining a failed condition, malformed data, and absent conditions, which differ in diagnostic and remedial meaning; reason 13 was absent, since "authorized executor does not match" presupposes an authorization exists; and reason 14 was absent, so an unmet independence requirement could not refuse unless the one-hop artifact test happened to trigger. EXCLUDED, EXPRESSLY: the three ABS-0004 Section 4.7 disclosure constraints are not checked by authorize() in this slice. They are not checkable from stored records: OutboundInteractionLog is in Section 11, Defined but Deferred, so no such record exists; EffectiveInputManifest carries completeness_attestation partial_declared_channels_only on every record, so a manifest attesting its own partiality cannot ground a refusal for undeclared configuration; and an undisclosed subordinate execution requires detecting an absence, which no stored record supplies. Reason 11 therefore reaches a subordinate that IS represented and exceeds its declared classes, and does not reach one never disclosed as an Invocation at all, which ABS-0004 Section 3 calls not an implicitly authorized act. An invocation with a required disclosure absent can pass every check in this slice and be classified governed. That is a stated limit of the slice, not a gap the fixtures will catch.

The one-hop self-adjudication check: for an adjudicator-authority role over a target artifact, if the artifact carries a produced_by relation to an InvocationRecord whose executed_by equals the executor under authorization, refuse. Scoped explicitly to one hop; multi-hop ancestry is Slice D.

Consequence classification per ABS-0004 Section 8: default by target type, effective consequence as the maximum of the default and applicable modifier levels, modifiers only raising, and downward adjustment only as a governed exception carrying reason, principal, scope, evidence, and review condition.

The experimental-versus-governed boundary: a classify function marking an invocation governed only when a valid authorization covers it, experimental otherwise. Classification only; no invocation is refused execution by this slice. "Valid authorization" here means only that an authorization record covers the invocation and none of the fourteen refusal reasons applies. It does not certify disclosure compliance, and a governed classification asserts nothing about whether ABS-0004 Section 4.7's constraints were met. Neither the documentation nor any summary may describe a governed result as a valid authorization under the full set of adopted ABS-0004 constraints, because the Section 4.7 constraints are excluded from what is checked.
Predicate-registry entries for the Slice C predicates: assigned_role, authorized_by, authorizes, qualifies_executor, qualifies_for, issued_under, based_on, approved_by.

Validator fixtures covering valid records, each rejection class, and each refusal reason, plus an integration fixture authorizing an invocation against stored role, qualification, and principal records offline.

Field reconciliation with ABS-0004 4.13: InvocationAuthorization carries the inherited DecisionRecord fields (target, recommended_status and effective_status, issuer invocation, accountable approver, evidence, policy authority, activation state, supersession) alongside its kind-specific fields, and the documentation states how issuing principal, issuer invocation, and accountable approver relate. COMP-0037 found the plan's field list and the ontology's inherited list unreconciled.

Self-issued marking per ABS-0004 v8: where the issuing principal and the authorized executor are the same party, the authorization records self_issued true. Self-issued authorizations are permitted and are disqualified from counting as independent authorization wherever independence is required.

The one-hop bound is recorded on the outcome: the self-adjudication result carries a check_depth field marking the check as direct-only. The field discloses the scope of the check that ran. It does not prevent a consumer from misreading a permitted result, and it carries no information about whether a deeper collision exists for the artifact in question: a two-hop-clean and a two-hop-colliding artifact both return permitted with the identical value. A permitted result establishes no general independence finding and does not exclude equivalent-executor conflicts further back in the evidence ancestry. Nothing in this slice prevents that misuse; only Slice D's ancestry traversal could establish or rule out such a conflict. The earlier wording claimed a consumer cannot misread the result, which asserted a control a field cannot provide and contradicted ABS-0004 P6, under which a label implying confirmation where none exists is a defect regardless of the correctness of its contents.
success_criteria: A stored invocation is classified governed when a valid authorization covers it and experimental otherwise, demonstrated by fixtures for both outcomes.

Each of the fourteen enumerated refusal reasons is exercised by a fixture and yields that reason; no fixture path returns a permitted outcome without a matching authorization record. This is enumerated-fixture coverage of the fourteen named reasons; it does not establish that no implementation path can return permitted without a matching authorization.

An authorization whose chain terminates nowhere is refused, and an authorization issued outside a principal's declared authority_scope is refused, each with its own reason. Checkable for the chain-termination case. The authority_scope case is checkable only against fixtures whose scopes are hand-constructed: ABS-0004 supplies no scope grammar and no matching semantics, so "outside its declared scope" cannot be evaluated in general.

The one-hop self-adjudication check refuses an adjudicator authorization over an artifact produced by the same executor identity, demonstrated against a real captured InvocationRecord, permits it when the identities differ, and carries a check_depth field marking the result as direct-only in both cases. The identity-collision logic and the presence and value of check_depth are mechanically checkable against any fixture InvocationRecord. The requirement to demonstrate against a real captured InvocationRecord is not: no record is named and no selection rule is given. The criterion is met by naming the specific InvocationRecord used.

Consequence classification is exercised over the enumerated modifier set: for each modifier, a fixture asserts the effective class equals the maximum of the default and the modifier level, and a downward adjustment without a recorded governed exception is refused. This is enumerated-fixture coverage of the named cases, not a proof of monotonicity over all inputs.

A qualification lacking an execution scope is rejected, and a qualification is not honoured for an endpoint or execution profile outside its scope. Checkable only against fixtures whose ExecutionProfile constraints are hand-constructed: ABS-0004 Section 4.6 gives the scope fields but no matching semantics for "permitted ExecutionProfile constraints" and no definition of a materially different profile.

A self-issued authorization is accepted, carries self_issued true, and is reported as not independent by any check that asks for independent authorization. Checkable under the plan's exact-identifier-equality rule for party sameness. "Any check that asks for independent authorization" is unbounded and is not checkable as written; the criterion is met against the enumerated checks this slice defines.

Regression: Slice A capture and Slice B resolution are unchanged, demonstrated by a fixture that runs both against stored records before and after authorization code is importable and asserts byte-identical outputs. COMP-0037 found this constraint had no corresponding check. Byte-identical output over the fixture set is unambiguous and checkable. It does not establish the broader constraint that no field, path, or default of Slice A or Slice B was altered.

The new modules are covered by tests exercising every public entrypoint and every enumerated outcome; the full suite passes offline with no network access. The offline-with-no-network condition is checkable as pass or fail. "Every public entrypoint" is not checkable as written: the criterion is met against an enumerated list of entrypoints recorded with the tests.

The repository audit reports ok true verified_current, and commit-level cross-environment reproduction from the public repository yields byte-identical checksums for every delivered file. Not mechanically checkable as written and restated as two conditions with named procedures: the audit reports ok true and verification_outcome verified_current when scripts/audit_self_model_index.py is run at the delivered commit; and a second clone of the public repository at that commit yields identical sha256 for each delivered file under a recorded file list. Without the procedure, the commands, and the semantics of verified_current, neither clause could be evaluated.
summary: Implement ABS-0004 v8 Slice C: RoleDefinition records on the three admitted axes, execution-scoped RoleQualification, InvocationAuthorization as a DecisionRecord kind, consequence classification, and the experimental-versus-governed boundary. An authorization is issued by an AccountablePrincipal holding standing authority within a declared scope, or chains to one; an authorization that chains to nothing is unauthorized rather than permitted. Authorization has one consequence in this slice and no others: an invocation is classified governed only when an authorization covers it, and experimental otherwise. Nothing is refused execution. The authorization function additionally performs a one-hop self-adjudication check using Slice A provenance: if the artifact under adjudication carries an InvocationRecord whose executor identity equals the executor being authorized, authorization is refused with an enumerated reason.
title: Roles, qualification, and invocation authorization (ABS-0004 Slice C)
